definitions.explanation: A traditional Japanese umbrella made of bamboo and oiled paper, characterized by a distinctive circular pattern resembling a snake's eye when viewed from above.

examples.japanese: {舞妓|まいこ}さんが{赤|あか}い{蛇|じゃ}の{目傘|めがさ}を{差|さ}している。
examples.english: The maiko is holding a red traditional umbrella.

examples.japanese: {蛇|じゃ}の{目傘|めがさ}は{和装|わそう}に{合|あ}う。
examples.english: Traditional paper umbrellas match well with Japanese clothing.

examples.japanese: {職人|しょくにん}が{一本|いっぽん}ずつ{手作|てづく}りした{蛇|じゃ}の{目傘|めがさ}。
examples.english: Traditional umbrellas handmade one by one by craftsmen.

notes:
ETYMOLOGY: {蛇|じゃ}の{目|め} (snake's eye) + {傘|かさ} (umbrella). Named for the concentric circular pattern on the umbrella that resembles a snake's eye.

STRUCTURE:
・Made of {竹|たけ} (bamboo) frame
・Covered with {和紙|わし} (Japanese paper)
・Waterproofed with {油|あぶら} (oil)
・Characteristic concentric circle pattern

RELATED UMBRELLA TYPES:
・{番傘|ばんがさ}: plain traditional umbrella (simpler design)
・{和傘|わがさ}: general term for Japanese traditional umbrellas
・{日傘|ひがさ}: parasol (for sun protection)
・{唐傘|からかさ}: Chinese-style umbrella

USAGE CONTEXTS:
・{茶道|さどう} (tea ceremony)
・{舞踊|ぶよう} (traditional dance)
・{結婚式|けっこんしき} (weddings - used for {和装|わそう})
・{写真撮影|しゃしんさつえい} (photo shoots with kimono)
・{旅館|りょかん} decorations

CULTURAL NOTE:
Traditional {蛇|じゃ}の{目傘|めがさ} are now mainly used for ceremonial purposes, photography, and as decorations, having been largely replaced by Western-style umbrellas for everyday use. They are handcrafted by skilled artisans, with famous production areas including Gifu and Kyoto.
